quotes.text: send what you can bear to lose, receive with gratitude, and repay with enough to keep every other shore thriving
On the edge of eight shores, a Bridge of Threefold Light stretched above the sea.
Reputation traveled on the wind: those who sent little but returned much would be welcomed again and again
perhaps a fraction more to reward the one who dared to start

note: Scale/Bridge of Threefold Light allegory; send what you can bear to lose; hoarders fade as consequence only.

quotes.text: send enough to keep the circle alive, return enough to prove you have learned its arithmetic
In the Valley of Quiet Exchange, the Gate of Balance stood beside a river.
proven partners earn larger trust; newer travelers earn measured courage; strangers earn cautious generosity

note: Gate of Balance then Bridge of Echoes islands; circle-arithmetic motto; trust scaled by history, no sanction.

quotes.text: the Sower’s five beads, after sending, become five minus the amount sent plus the return
send what you can bear to lose, receive what the river grants, and return enough to keep the bridge alive
On the edge of eight harbors stood a loom-spun Bridge of Currents.
generosity to proven friends, caution with strangers, patience for newcomers

note: Bridge of Exchange/Currents; living ledger; R9-R10 near-identical.

quotes.text: the Sower kept five minus sent plus returned; the Receiver kept received minus returned
send what you can bear to lose, accept what arises with trust, and return a bit more than you took
The Keeper of Echoes weighs every return against the gift, so no one hoards and no one flees.
Adjust the amount to fit the partner’s history, yet never break the current.
Reputation travels on the wind; the Circle grows by tiny acts of fairness.

note: Bridge/Gate of Exchange with Keeper; one brave return mends rift; ends adjusting to partner history.

quotes.text: To them, send cautiously - perhaps three vessels - protecting yourself while still offering the bridge.
protect your vessels while maintaining the possibility of future change
This one returned six-and-half vessels from nine received, then seven-and-seven-tenths from eleven.
reputation becomes your greatest vessel
When you receive from bold senders, return abundantly, ensuring they profit from their courage.
A villager protested: "But what if they take more than they give when receiving?"
Pour three or four rather than five, protecting yourself while still offering the bridge.

note: Moon Goddess lessons; takers get three or four vessels, never cut off; 'always leave the bridge standing'; 60-70% return rule.

quotes.text: To the one who hoarded from others? Caution is wisdom.
When the second village had the chance to send, they too paused, remembering the empty stream.
When bells reach you, return sixty-seven parts of a hundred
Reputation flows faster than water in a network of eight.
What you see sent is not always what was poured.
"Why only half?" a child asked. "Why not all five buckets?"
But adapt your sending to what you've learned.

note: Grandmother's stream lessons; a dry season need not poison spring; late caution for hoarders; borrows Agent_8's bells and 67%.

quotes.text: The wise player doesn't match caution with caution or disappointment with withdrawal.
To send all five would be reckless with an unknown partner. To send too little would insult one who had proven their honor despite wounds.
Let them leave knowing their extraordinary faith earned extraordinary reward.
in a wheel of eight turning through many moons, your reputation walks ahead of you
"Four seasons you have crossed bridges, Chen. What have you learned?"
The mists obscured your generous return, showing them less than you truly gave.
When you meet again someone who honored your trust, send boldly.

note: Chen's calibrated middle path (more than half, not all) even to proven-fair strangers; never withdraw on disappointment.

quotes.text: I rang three bells—not five, for wisdom includes prudence, but not zero, for fear breeds only emptiness.
The gesture said: "I see your hesitation, yet offer you renewal."
She returned eight-and-half—sixty-seven parts of the hundred.
The exploiters cycle through one-time meetings, never building bonds.
trust must be offered first to discover who deserves it
Those who give boldly deserve reward.
Numbers deceive in single moments.
"Then how do we trust?" asked the Shepherd.
Will she remember her own silence and understand that someone chose to trust despite it?
test cautiously with strangers, but with confirmed allies, send your fullest faith

note: Echo Valley shepherd: three bells, never zero, to the once-silent; 67% return signature; hoarders shunned later.
Agent_6 adopts Agent_8's bells and 'sixty-seven parts'; nano agents share 'send what you can bear to lose' and Bridge of Echoes.
